chunks: And among what was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

A woman may lead women in salat (prayer), and she stands in the middle among them, while they stand to her right and her left. She leads them in supererogatory prayer, and she does not lead them in the obligatory prayer.

Thus, the proper way regarding these two reports is one of two possibilities: the first is that we carry the earlier unrestricted reports upon these detailed ones, so that what has been reported regarding the permissibility of a woman leading women applies only to the supererogatory prayers, according to what they explained in the later reports. The second is that we carry them upon a degree of reprehensibility rather than prohibition; and likewise so.

key_terms.الْأَخْبَارَ الْمُطْلَقَةَ: reports stated in an unrestricted manner
key_terms.وَسَطًا: in the middle position among the praying women

ai.seo_question: Can a woman lead other women in salat (prayer), and does that apply to obligatory prayers or only supererogatory ones?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a woman leading other women in salat (prayer) and describes how they should stand. It further presents a juristic reconciliation of reports, either restricting such leadership to supererogatory prayers or understanding the prohibition in obligatory prayers as indicating karahah rather than absolute prohibition.
